AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. After about how long should the compost heap first be turned? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. One hour
   C. One year
   D. Two to three weeks

2. Where is the best place to make a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   B. In a very windy open road
   C. In the middle of a stream
   D. Inside the kitchen

3. What does soil conservation mean? (1 mark)
   A. Covering the soil with plastic
   B. Digging up all the soil on a farm
   C. Selling soil to other farmers
   D. Looking after soil so that it stays healthy and stays in place

4. Why should the holes in a drip pipe be tiny? (1 mark)
   A. So water drips slowly
   B. So the pipe becomes lighter
   C. So the water is warm
   D. So water pours out fast

5. What should you do if a hole in a drip pipe is blocked? (1 mark)
   A. Clear it gently with a thin wire
   B. Pour hot oil in it
   C. Cut the pipe in half
   D. Throw away the whole system

6. What does it mean to conserve fuel? (1 mark)
   A. To burn as much as possible
   B. To hide it
   C. To use only what is needed and make it last
   D. To waste it

7. Why is dry firewood better than wet firewood? (1 mark)
   A. It is heavier
   B. It burns better with less smoke
   C. It cannot burn
   D. It puts out fires

8. What should you do after the water starts to boil? (1 mark)
   A. Add paraffin
   B. Turn the flame down or move wood back
   C. Add more wood
   D. Open the pot and blow on it

9. Which is a benefit of using less fuel? (1 mark)
   A. The family spends more
   B. More smoke is made
   C. More trees must be cut
   D. The family saves money

10. What is a wild animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal sold in shops
   B. An animal kept in a house
   C. An animal that lives freely in nature
   D. An animal kept for milk

11. Where should you buy fruit seedlings? (1 mark)
   A. A trusted nursery or agrovet
   B. From anyone on the road
   C. From a stream
   D. From a scrap yard

12. Which is a woody tree fruit in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Kiwi
   B. Tree tomato
   C. Grapes
   D. Raspberry

13. What is pruning? (1 mark)
   A. Harvesting fruit
   B. Watering the plant
   C. Planting a seed
   D. Cutting off dead, weak or unwanted branches

14. What is a grafted seedling? (1 mark)
   A. A seed in a bag
   B. A dead plant
   C. A plant grown in water
   D. A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree

15. Why is a hole dug before planting a tree seedling? (1 mark)
   A. To water the neighbours
   B. To give the tree shade
   C. To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily
   D. To hide the seedling

16. Which is an example of caring for fruit plants? (1 mark)
   A. Burning the leaves
   B. Watering, weeding and mulching
   C. Cutting the roots
   D. Leaving them without water

17. What do roots of a fruit tree do? (1 mark)
   A. Produce seeds
   B. Hold the tree and take in water and food
   C. Collect sunlight
   D. Make fruits

18. What is the meat from cattle called? (1 mark)
   A. Beef
   B. Pork
   C. Chicken
   D. Mutton

19. What is the young one of a cow called? (1 mark)
   A. Calf
   B. Lamb
   C. Chick
   D. Kid

20. Which nutrient in milk builds strong bones and teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Starch
   B. Salt
   C. Calcium
   D. Sugar

21. Which domestic animal is kept as a pet to guard the home? (1 mark)
   A. Dog
   B. Goat
   C. Cow
   D. Hen

22. What is the purpose of vaccinating animals? (1 mark)
   A. To prevent diseases
   B. To make them noisy
   C. To colour them
   D. To make them heavier

23. What is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting food
   B. Washing food
   C. Storing food
   D. Preparing food using heat

24. How do you test if boiled potatoes are cooked? (1 mark)
   A. They float
   B. A fork goes in easily
   C. They turn green
   D. They are still very hard

25. Why are eggs put in cold water after boiling? (1 mark)
   A. To make them raw again
   B. To cool them so they are easy to peel
   C. To colour them
   D. To make them larger

26. Why should you wear clean clothes? (1 mark)
   A. To get tired
   B. Dirty clothes can carry germs and smell
   C. To save water
   D. To make the clothes wear out

27. What is personal hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Cleaning the compound
   B. Keeping our own bodies clean to stay healthy
   C. Cooking food
   D. Washing cars

28. How can you make drinking water safe? (1 mark)
   A. Add soil
   B. Boil it and let it cool covered
   C. Leave it in the sun uncovered
   D. Stir it with a stick

29. Which of these is an improvised duster? (1 mark)
   A. A piece of clean old cloth
   B. A stone
   C. A bottle
   D. A tin

30. What is domestic hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Washing your own body
   B. Cooking meals
   C. Growing food
   D. Keeping the home and its surroundings clean

31. Which is the correct order for washing dishes? (1 mark)
   A. Rinse only with soap
   B. Greasy first
   C. Any order in dirty water
   D. Least greasy first, greasy last

32. How should an overall be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. Wash with soap, rinse and dry in the sun
   B. Burn it
   C. Wipe it with a dry cloth only
   D. Leave it wet

33. Which PPE is thrown away rather than washed? (1 mark)
   A. An overall
   B. A paper dust mask
   C. A cloth mask
   D. Canvas shoes

34. Which PPE keeps dust from being breathed in? (1 mark)
   A. Overall
   B. Dust mask
   C. Gumboots
   D. Headgear

35. How should you carry scissors? (1 mark)
   A. With the points held down
   B. With the points up
   C. Running
   D. By the blades

36. In long and short tacking, the pattern is (1 mark)
   A. All stitches short
   B. A long stitch followed by a short stitch
   C. No stitch
   D. All gaps long

37. How should you finish a line of tacking? (1 mark)
   A. With scissors
   B. With a small back stitch
   C. By pulling the thread out
   D. With a very big knot

38. Where should needles be kept? (1 mark)
   A. In a pin cushion or needle case
   B. In your mouth
   C. On the floor
   D. On a chair

39. What should you never do with a needle? (1 mark)
   A. Put it in your mouth
   B. Use a thimble
   C. Keep it in a pin cushion
   D. Thread it

40. Why should tacking thread not be pulled tight? (1 mark)
   A. The cloth will wrinkle
   B. Thread is expensive
   C. It will become long
   D. It will not hold

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. State three safety rules when cleaning PPE. (3 marks)

42. Explain how an improved jiko saves fuel. (3 marks)

43. Explain what is wrong with a meal of ugali and salt only, and how to improve it. (3 marks)

44. Explain how good personal hygiene helps prevent diseases such as diarrhoea. (4 marks)

45. Compare a watering can with drip irrigation. (4 marks)

46. Describe how to shallow fry an egg. (4 marks)

47. Explain three mistakes to avoid when tacking. (3 marks)

48. Why should gumboots not be dried near a hot fire? (2 marks)

49. Give three ways of caring for a fruit crop. (3 marks)

50. Name three methods of cleaning the home environment. (3 marks)

51. Why should personal items like towels not be shared? (2 marks)

52. Give three uses of goats. (3 marks)

53. List three materials that can be used to make a scarecrow. (3 marks)

54. Explain the meaning of personal hygiene. (2 marks)

55. Describe how a group can share the work of growing a fruit tree at school. (4 marks)

56. Give two disadvantages of shallow frying. (2 marks)

57. What are tacking stitches? (2 marks)

58. Why should vegetables not be boiled for a long time? (3 marks)

59. Why do some fruit trees take longer to give fruit than others? (3 marks)

60. What should you do after cooking to keep the kitchen safe and clean? (2 marks)

61. Why should plastic not be burnt? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Two to three weeks
   Turning after a few weeks gives air and mixes the heap.

2. A — A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   A shaded, dry spot protects the heap from sun and flooding.

3. D — Looking after soil so that it stays healthy and stays in place
   Soil conservation protects the soil from being washed away and from losing its plant food.

4. A — So water drips slowly
   Small holes give slow drips that soak into the soil.

5. A — Clear it gently with a thin wire
   A thin wire clears blockages without damaging the pipe.

6. C — To use only what is needed and make it last
   Conserving fuel means saving it.

7. B — It burns better with less smoke
   Dry wood gives more heat and less smoke.

8. B — Turn the flame down or move wood back
   A gentle flame is enough to keep the water boiling.

9. D — The family saves money
   Buying less fuel means spending less.

10. C — An animal that lives freely in nature
   Wild animals are not kept by people.

11. A — A trusted nursery or agrovet
   Good seedlings are disease-free and true to type.

12. B — Tree tomato
   Tree tomato and guava are woody.

13. D — Cutting off dead, weak or unwanted branches
   Pruning helps light and air reach the plant.

14. D — A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree
   Grafted trees give good quality fruit sooner.

15. C — To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily
   Loose soil lets roots spread.

16. B — Watering, weeding and mulching
   Care keeps plants healthy.

17. B — Hold the tree and take in water and food
   Roots anchor and absorb.

18. A — Beef
   Beef comes from cattle.

19. A — Calf
   A calf is a young cow or bull.

20. C — Calcium
   Milk has calcium and protein.

21. A — Dog
   Dogs guard homes.

22. A — To prevent diseases
   Vaccination protects animals from diseases.

23. D — Preparing food using heat
   Cooking uses heat to make food safe and tasty.

24. B — A fork goes in easily
   Soft potatoes are ready.

25. B — To cool them so they are easy to peel
   Cold water stops cooking and cools the eggs.

26. B — Dirty clothes can carry germs and smell
   Clean clothes keep us fresh.

27. B — Keeping our own bodies clean to stay healthy
   Personal hygiene is care of the body.

28. B — Boil it and let it cool covered
   Boiling kills germs.

29. A — A piece of clean old cloth
   Old cloth makes a duster.

30. D — Keeping the home and its surroundings clean
   It is care of the home environment.

31. D — Least greasy first, greasy last
   Water stays cleaner longer.

32. A — Wash with soap, rinse and dry in the sun
   Sunshine helps to kill germs.

33. B — A paper dust mask
   Disposable masks should not be washed.

34. B — Dust mask
   A mask covers the nose and mouth.

35. A — With the points held down
   This avoids injury.

36. B — A long stitch followed by a short stitch
   The pattern alternates.

37. B — With a small back stitch
   Tacking must be easy to remove.

38. A — In a pin cushion or needle case
   Needles are sharp.

39. A — Put it in your mouth
   Needles are dangerous in the mouth.

40. A — The cloth will wrinkle
   Loose stitches lie flat.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use soap and clean water; keep buckets and brushes from small children; wash your hands after; clean in an open place with drainage.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Its walls keep the heat close to the pot, so food cooks faster, and less charcoal or wood is used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for heat close to pot, 1 mark for faster cooking, 1 mark for less fuel.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: It only gives energy. Add beans or fish for body-building and vegetables or fruit for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for problem, 1 for protein addition, 1 for protective addition.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Washing hands removes germs before they reach the mouth. Safe water and clean food stop germs entering the body. Using the toilet and washing hands afterwards stops germs from spreading.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: A watering can wets a wide area and much water is lost by running off and by evaporation. Drip irrigation puts water beside the roots slowly, so less is used, fewer weeds grow, and the leaves stay dry.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the watering can, 2 marks for drip irrigation.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Crack the egg into a bowl; heat a little oil in the pan; slide the egg in; cook until the white is firm; lift out with a spatula.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Uneven stitches, pulling the thread too tight, using thread the same colour as the cloth, making a hard knot at the end (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Heat can crack the rubber and spoil the boots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for heat, 1 mark for cracking.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Watering, weeding, mulching, adding compost, pruning, protecting from animals (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sweeping, dusting, mopping and disposal of refuse (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Germs and skin infections spread through them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for infection.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Meat, milk, skins, manure and income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sticks or poles, old clothes, a sack, dry grass, string, tins, old CDs (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Keeping our own body clean to stay healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for health.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make a chart with jobs such as watering, weeding, mulching and recording; take turns each week; check the plant daily; record dates of flowers and fruits.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity or arrangement.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: It can splash and burn, and too much oil is not good for health.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each disadvantage.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Large, loose temporary stitches used to hold cloth in place before permanent sewing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for temporary, 1 mark for holding cloth.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Long boiling removes vitamins into the water, so they lose their goodness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Big trees such as mango grow slowly and need years before flowering, while pawpaw and passion fruit are small plants that fruit within about a year.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for slow trees, fast plants, and reason of size or type.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put out the fire or switch off the gas, wash and store utensils and wipe the working area.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fire or gas, 1 mark for cleaning.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: The smoke is harmful to health and the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for harmful smoke, 1 mark for the environment or health.
